# Show and tell: what you built on a TI board, and what the code did there

Terms: [docs/vocab.md](https://github.com/Fox-Red-Labs/fox-red-labs/blob/main/docs/vocab.md).

Post a build here, or ask a question in [Q&A](https://github.com/Fox-Red-Labs/fox-red-labs/discussions/categories/q-a). Pick a category, then fill in the form.

## What a post should have

1. **What you built or ported.** A line or two, and the project it started from.
2. **What it runs on.** The kit (its board id is the folder name), and the SDK or tool version.
3. **A photo, a clip or a log.** Something that shows it running.
4. **Anything that did not work.** Optional, and the most useful part.

A post with all four parts can be repeated by the next person.

## What to expect

- Credit that lasts. When a post leads to a fix, the fix goes into the board's `FAQ.md` or `AGENTS.md` under your GitHub handle, and your handle joins the Built-by list for that board. Write "anonymous" in the post to opt out.
- A step that failed, with the exact error text, belongs in the [Report a problem](https://github.com/Fox-Red-Labs/fox-red-labs/issues/new?template=broke-here.yml) form. It becomes a report on that board's page and, once repeated on the bench, a fix.

## Ground rules

Public sources only. Facts about other vendors' products, or nothing. Say "builds", "flashes", "runs" or "verified", whichever happened. Your project stays yours.

The guide with all of this: [docs/how-to-contribute.md](https://github.com/Fox-Red-Labs/fox-red-labs/blob/main/docs/how-to-contribute.md).
